components.text: Demonstrate that the asserted causal regress is impossible and that its required actual terminus is adequately identifiable as God.
Show why contingent existence requires a necessary being rather than another structure of dependence.
Show why natural regularity requires purposeful direction by an intelligent mind.
Show that objective obligations exist and uniquely require a divine intellectual source.
Whether the asserted causal regress requires a transcendent actual source identifiable as God.
Whether contingent existence requires a necessary being rather than another explanatory stopping point.
Whether natural regularity warrants inference to purposeful direction by an intelligent mind.
Whether objective moral obligation requires existence in a divine intellect.
Establish or defeat the specific inference from observed causal dependence to a transcendent actual source identified as God.
Whether the offered metaphysical inference supplies enough evidence to warrant belief in God.
Whether the necessary-being argument overcomes rational and revisable withholding of belief.
Whether the natural-order argument provides evidence sufficient to alter nonbelief.
Whether the moral-law argument provides evidence sufficient to alter nonbelief.
Demonstrate that objective moral obligations exist and that their existence requires the divine intellect asserted by the affirmative.
Whether lawlike natural behavior demonstrates a directing divine mind despite persistent nonbelief.
Show that stable natural patterns are best explained by a purposeful directing mind rather than by nonmental regularity.
Whether stable natural regularity warrants a directing mind rather than merely reported personal communication.
Determine whether withholding belief carries the same positive evidential burden as asserting God's existence or a substantive contrary ontology.
Address the distinction between tentative evidence-based nonbelief and a positive assertion that no God exists.
Whether only the affirmative theistic claimant bears a burden in this debate.
Whether tentative nonbelief may simply await adequate affirmative evidence without defending a contrary explanation.
Justify extending causal principles from accessible intracosmic chains to a transcendent or temporally external explanatory source.
Establish that contingency reasoning applies beyond accessible reality and requires a necessary terminus.
Whether causal relations observed within nature license a necessary transcendent source beyond the accessible universe and temporal domain.
Whether observed dependent existence licenses extrapolation to a necessary being beyond accessible cosmological conditions.
Show that any required first actual cause possesses the agency, mentality, timelessness, and other attributes needed to count as God.
Connect a necessary existence, if established, to a thinking divine agent rather than an unspecified foundation.
Demonstrate that descriptive laws were created by a mind rather than merely characterizing regularities.
Whether an inferred first actual source is sufficiently connected to God and specifically to a timeless thinking agent.
Whether a necessary or foundational being is thereby shown to possess the divine attributes at issue.
Whether descriptive laws of nature require creation by a mind.
Provide independent grounds admitting a directing supernatural mind as a genuine explanatory candidate for natural regularity.
Whether an undemonstrated intelligent supernatural director may be included as the best explanation of natural regularity.
Show that explanatory incompleteness independently raises a supernatural directing mind to plausibility rather than merely leaving the cause unknown.
Whether lack of a known natural account for cosmic origins makes a supernatural causal explanation evidentially plausible.
Whether unanswered cosmological questions independently support a necessary supernatural being.
Whether acknowledged ignorance creates a reciprocal burden to disprove the proposed supernatural explanation.
Justify admitting God or a supernatural reality as a constrained candidate in an inference to the best explanation.
Identify positive evidence for the supernatural conclusion beyond the absence of a currently known natural explanation.
Whether God may be considered as an abductive explanatory candidate for observed natural effects.
Whether the Five Ways infer from positive observations rather than merely substitute God for ignorance.
Whether inference from observed natural effects illegitimately extrapolates beyond accessible conditions.
Explain how objective moral assessment can proceed from stated standards and physical facts without locating morality in a divine intellect.
Address whether divine moral grounding is a better explanatory inference than secular standards.
Whether objective moral assessment requires a divine intellect rather than a stated secular standard plus physical facts.
Whether atheists lack an accountable alternative treatment of alleged objective moral evidence.
Address the explicitly tentative position that belief is withheld for insufficient evidence and remains open to revision.
Distinguish the burden borne by positive metaphysical naturalism from the absence of belief in an asserted God.
Whether atheism in this debate is only tentative withholding of belief or a substantive metaphysical position.
Whether atheists avoid positive burdens merely by describing their stance as lack of belief.
Explain whether objective facts relative to well-being establish morality beyond adopted human standards or preferences.
Show why moral objectivity requires a foundation beyond human agreement and why that foundation avoids equivalent arbitrariness.
Whether objective moral wrongness can be preserved by factual assessment relative to a human well-being standard.
Whether morality can rest on an agreed human foundation without invoking standards beyond opinion.
Explain why knowledge of a personal God need not always take the form of publicly demonstrable or scientifically testable evidence.
Provide criteria distinguishing genuine interpersonal divine knowledge from mistaken or unfalsifiable reported communication.
Whether warranted knowledge of God must take the form of publicly demonstrable or scientifically testable evidence.
Whether interpersonal religious experience remains evidentially responsible when alleged communications are false or outcome-insensitive.
Whether interpersonal analogy supplies public evidence meeting the affirmative motion burden.
